expectations.text: Every class that inherits from the declarative Base is identified as an entity
expectations.evidence: detected-entities.json has User, Order, Role — all three Base-inheriting classes.

expectations.text: Each entity's table_name matches its own __tablename__ assignment (R3 per-class windowing)
relationship() declarations have type AND target_entity populated (T1)
expectations.evidence: T1 PROOF: User.relationship('Order') → target_entity='Order'; User.relationship('Role') → target_entity='Role'; Order.relationship('User') → target_entity='User'. All populated.

expectations.text: ForeignKey() declarations resolve to a target table name (not 'table.column') (T1)
expectations.evidence: T1 PROOF: Order.ForeignKey('users.id') → target_entity='users' (collapsed to table part, not 'users.id').

expectations.text: detected-entities.json serializes each relationship as {type, target_entity} (T2, not a bare kind string)
expectations.evidence: T2 PROOF: jq shows each relationship as {type: 'relationship'|'foreign_key', target_entity: 'Order'|'Role'|'User'|'users'}. Object shape, not flat kind strings.

expectations.text: Mermaid erDiagram has edges between real tables (users↔orders, users↔roles) with NO _rel placeholders
expectations.evidence: 4 edges: users||--o{ orders, users||--o{ roles, orders||--o{ users, orders}o--|| users. No `_rel` in grep. Real tables at both endpoints.

eval_feedback.overall: T1 + T2 both verified on SQLAlchemy. Every relationship has a resolved target_entity; JSON serializes them; Mermaid references real tables. The iteration-5 'points to _rel placeholders' caveat is now gone.
